subject: CloudMart renewal — pricing lock & commit ceiling discussion
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@cloudmart.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudmart.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — 12 month commit, request for pricing lock and burst allowance

Hi Jasmine,

Hope you're well — we're coming up on the end of our 12 month term and I wanted to start the renewal conversation early so we can avoid any service interruptions. High level: CloudMart is looking to renew for another 12 months and increase our committed capacity by ~35% to support the peak season. Given current market dynamics we also want a short-term pricing lock (90 days) on the base rate while our procurement reviews the PO.

Can Redwood grant a temporary pricing hold and a burst pool for seasonal spikes? If possible, please include any available credit for early commit and a short summary of options (discount tiers, credits, invoice timing). I've attached our internal usage report for the last quarter.

Thanks — Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Infrastructure
CloudMart

Attachment: cloudmart_usage_report_Q3.csv (csv)
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion — 12 month commit, request for pricing lock and burst allowance

Ben / Laura — forwarding Amit's note. CloudMart wants a 12-month renewal, +35% committed capacity, and a 90-day pricing lock while they get PO approval. They also asked for a burst pool and any early-commit credit.

Questions for pricing:
- Can we offer a 90-day price lock for the current base unit price if they sign a statement of intent (SOI) now?
- What credit structure would we propose for a 35% uplift on commit (one-time credit vs. monthly amortized)?
- Suggested burst pool (e.g., 15% monthly burst with overage at pay-as-you-go) and whether we need a tiered surcharge.

I've attached their usage report. I can loop in sales ops if you want a formal term sheet. Need your recommended numbers to share with Amit by Friday.

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: cloudmart_usage_report_Q3.csv (forwarded)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion — 12 month commit, request for pricing lock and burst allowance

Jasmine — thanks for the flag. High-level proposal below (numbers are illustrative; final will be in term sheet):

Option A — Anchor + Burst (recommended for renewal):
- 12 month commit: +35% vs current run-rate (committed token/embedding units).
- Discount: 18% off list on committed usage (applies to baseline usage up to commit).
- Early-commit credit: one-time credit equal to 6% of first-month committed invoice (applied as invoice credit).
- Pricing lock: 90 days from SOI signature; requires a non-binding SOI and PO submission within that window.
- Burst pool: 15% monthly burst included (no additional charge up to burst cap). Overage beyond burst billed at pay-as-you-go list rate.

Option B — Conservative (smaller upfront credit, lower discount):
- 12 month commit: +35%
- Discount: 12% off list
- Early-commit credit: 3% one-time credit
- Pricing lock: 60 days
- Burst: pay-as-you-go only, with 10% surcharge for spikes >25% sustained over 3 days

Operational notes:
- We should include a shortfall true-up clause at year-end (standard).
- For procurement/legal: provide a pre-filled term sheet + DocuSign link.
- If they want invoice timing adjusted (net45 -> net60) we can trade a 1-2% concession.

I've drafted a term sheet and attached a redline (CloudMart_TermSheet_v2.pdf). If you and Laura approve, I'll send to Amit with the SOI template and DocuSign link.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Director, EMEA & NA
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CloudMart_TermSheet_v2.pdf (redline), pricing_model_draft.xlsx (internal, not attached here)
From: Amit Shah <amit@cloudmart.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudmart.com>, legal@cloudmart.com
Date: Mon, 12 Sep 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — 12 month commit, request for pricing lock and burst allowance

Jasmine / Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarity. CloudMart is aligned with Option A in principle. Procurement wants the SOI + term sheet and will aim to have PO in 45 days. The 90-day lock meets our needs. Couple of asks before we sign the SOI:

- Can the early-commit credit be shown on the initial invoice as a line-item credit? Procurement prefers clear line items for accounting.
- We need the burst pool spelled out in the term sheet with an example calculation (how a 20% unexpected spike in week 8 would be billed).
- Please confirm the true-up cadence and whether usage reports are available via API for our finance tools.

If you can send the DocuSign link and the SOI PDF with the line-item credit visible, procurement can route the PO. We'll countersign as soon as legal expedites.

Thanks — Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Infrastructure
CloudMart
